bodyHtml:
10.2 Account, Mailbox, Metrics, and Trade History

Why This Matters

Beginners often open the account area and see many numbers without knowing which ones describe the present, which ones describe the past, and which ones are warnings.

This lesson makes the account side of the app easier to read. It also shows you how Mailbox and Trade History fit into the same review workflow.

What You Should Understand After This Lesson

By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:

  • switch between Account and Mailbox;
  • read the main account cards without guessing;
  • understand what stale pricing means;
  • filter and review Trade History with the correct on-screen controls.

The Two Panels Inside Account

When you open the Account tab, you can switch between:

  • Account
  • Mailbox

Think of them this way:

  • Account shows your numbers, summaries, and insights
  • Mailbox shows your messages and replies

The Account Information Card

The first card is titled Account Information on larger screens and Account Info on smaller screens.

It shows:

  • Username
  • Account Type
  • Member Since
  • Open Positions

This card answers the basic question, "Whose account is this, and what is open right now?"

The Main Metric Cards

The metric strip uses these exact labels:

  • Balance
  • Equity
  • Free Margin
  • Used Margin
  • Floating P/L
  • Margin Level

Here is the beginner-friendly meaning of each:

Label Plain-English meaning
Balance Your account value before adding open profit or loss
Equity Your account value after including open profit or loss
Free Margin Margin still available for trading
Used Margin Margin already tied up by current positions
Floating P/L Profit or loss from trades that are still open
Margin Level A percentage that shows how safe or stretched the account is

(Table alt-text: A six-row table translating the account metric-card labels into plain beginner language.)

Stale Pricing Warnings

Sometimes account values are not updating from fresh market prices.

When that happens, the app can show a warning that says:

P/L and margin values are frozen due to stale or missing price data ... Trading and closing may be blocked until fresh quotes are available.

For a beginner, the message means:

  • some values may be temporarily frozen
  • the account screen is warning you for safety
  • you should not treat frozen numbers as fully current

Trading Statistics and Trader Insights

Below the main metric cards, the Account screen also shows:

  • Trading Statistics
  • Trader Insights

Inside those areas, you may see labels such as:

  • Total Trades
  • Winning
  • Losing
  • Win Rate
  • Total Realized P/L
  • Most Profitable Instrument
  • Least Profitable Instrument
  • Best Direction
  • Best Trading Hour
  • Optimal Holding Time
  • All Instruments Performance

These sections are review tools. They are not buttons you must press before every trade.

The Trading Journal Shortcut

Near the bottom of the account page, there is also a quick-access card titled Trading Journal.

Its description says:

Document your trades, emotions, and lessons learned

If you tap it, the app takes you to the dedicated journal route.

Using Mailbox

When you switch to Mailbox, the main title is Mailbox.

Important visible labels include:

  • Threads
  • category choices All, System, Support, Announcement, Challenges
  • Reply format
  • reply choices Plain text and Markdown
  • Send Reply

Useful status messages include:

  • Loading mailbox…
  • No messages yet.
  • Select a thread
  • Select a thread to read messages.
  • No messages in this thread.

If replies are not available, the app can show:

  • Messaging is currently disabled by admin.
  • Replies are disabled for this thread.

Using Trade History

The History tab opens the page titled Trade History.

At the top, you can filter what you see using:

  • the search box Search...
  • the dropdown Symbol
  • the dropdown Time
  • the dropdown Reason

The Time dropdown currently includes:

  • Today
  • 7 days
  • 30 days
  • 90 days
  • All
  • Custom...

If you choose Custom..., the date-range tool uses:

  • the title Select date range
  • the buttons Cancel and Apply

Reading the History Table

The sortable table uses labels such as:

  • Ticket
  • Symbol
  • Open Price
  • Close Price
  • Profit/Loss
  • Duration
  • Close Reason

That makes Trade History different from Mailbox:

  • Mailbox is for messages
  • Trade History is for completed trades
learningOutcomes: read the main `Account` metrics without guessing what each card means;
switch between the `Account` and `Mailbox` panels confidently;
use the `Trade History` filters and understand the custom date-range flow;
recognize stale-data warnings, empty states, and journal quick-access links.
